# Implement block: Unlocking Checkout Steps (React Native)

You are adding the "Unlocking Checkout Steps" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

The confirming steps of a checkout on white: the title "Confirm", three step dots (a green check, a black "2" with "DELIVERY DETAILS", a grey "3") and the order's card with "Order 12329", "$19.11", "Placed on 3 June 2022" and a large square button, grey with a down arrow. A light grey drawer under the card asks one thing at a time: "SELECT AN OPTION" with Delivery and Pickup, where the suggested one sits in a grey pill that turns black when tapped; that unfolds "DELIVERY BY", a strip of hours whose middle pill turns black the same way; and that unfolds "DELIVERY TO" with "Home" and a teal "Change", at which the card's button turns green and its arrow turns to the right. Confirm folds the drawer away while the two black picks fly up to the card's right side, the option landing as plain words and the hour as a pill; the price greys, the card grows to show the address over a street map on which a teal route draws itself, the third dot takes over and a green "Done" appears. Done grows into a green sheet that takes the whole screen, on which a drawn parcel with a check badge, "Checkout successful!" and a black "Return to Dashboard" scale up; returning puts the form back as it started.

**Motion.** A tapped option or hour fills from grey to black in 180 ms, dips to 0.9 in 90 ms and bounces back on a spring (damping 8, stiffness 320, mass 0.8); the option pill slides between the two options on a spring (damping 17, stiffness 240). 180 ms after a choice the next section unfolds on a spring (damping 17, stiffness 150, a little overshoot): the drawer grows by the section's height (138 pt, then 136 pt, under the first 118 pt) while its content fades in from 20% to 90% of the way. With the hour chosen the button goes from grey to green and its arrow from down to right in 380 ms (ease-out cubic). The arrows of the strip step the hour and a tap on a neighbouring hour brings it to the middle and chooses it; labels cross-fade (180 ms in, 120 ms out). Confirm runs one spring from 0 to 1 (damping 18, stiffness 130): the drawer's height goes to nothing and it fades between 20% and 70%; the option pill travels from the drawer to 26 pt inside the card's right edge, 32 pt from its top, shrinking from 122 × 58 to 86 × 24 while its black fades out by 80% and its label turns dark; the hour pill travels to 68 pt from the top, 82 pt wide, going from 58 to 48 pt high; the card grows from 160 pt to the summary's height, the button and the rule fade out in the first 40%, the address row and map fade in from 45%, the second dot becomes a check and its name closes up as the third dot turns black and its name opens; Done fades in from 60% and rises 18 pt; 350 ms later the route draws over 700 ms (ease-in-out cubic). The second dot goes back to the choices along the same spring. Done runs a 520 ms clock (ease-in-out cubic): the green sheet takes the screen's width in the first 40% and its height from 8% to 100% while a copy of the label grows to 2.6 times and fades between 15% and 70%; from 70% the drawing, title and button fade in and scale up from 0.7 on a spring (damping 13, stiffness 150), and 200 ms after the flood the check draws in 320 ms. "Return to Dashboard" resets the form behind the green and fades it out in 360 ms. Buttons give a light haptic. The self-playing demo loops every 10 s with no haptics, each press shown for 150 ms first: Delivery at 0.8 s, the hour at 2 s, Confirm at 3.6 s, Done at 5.6 s and "Return to Dashboard" at 8.2 s; a touch takes over and 3 s after the last one the form goes back to its start (in 300 ms) and the loop begins again. Under reduced motion sections open in 160 ms and the summary in 200 ms without springs, nothing bounces or rises, and the success screen fades in without scaling.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/forms/unlocking-checkout-steps/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [CheckoutArt.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/forms/unlocking-checkout-steps/CheckoutArt.tsx)
- [UnlockingCheckoutSteps.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/forms/unlocking-checkout-steps/UnlockingCheckoutSteps.tsx)

### Packages

- `@expo/vector-icons`
- `@shopify/react-native-skia`
- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-status-bar`
- `react-native-reanimated`
- `react-native-safe-area-context`
- `react-native-worklets`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
